reasoning: Both attempts implement every rule correctly and reject garbage input safely. B wins on comments and typing. Its comments are short and each one explains a reason, and its tagged-union result type is cleaner than A's tuple. A opens with a boilerplate header block and has wordier comment blocks. A's GetPartBoundsInBox overlap check is somewhat more robust than B's loop over direct children, but that matters less than the gap in comment quality, which most of the rubric weighs.

criteria.note: `check` covers every rule: it validates the five types, snaps to cells starting at GROUND_Y = 0, rejects `cell.Y - HALF < GROUND_Y` and `cell.Y + HALF > GROUND_Y + MAX_HEIGHT`, enforces 24-stud reach, and runs GetPartBoundsInBox with a 3.8-stud box so touching neighbours pass; `snap` and `snapFromHit` are exposed.
Type checks come first, then `isFiniteNumber` (n == n and abs ~= huge) on each component, then a second finiteness check after snapping, all before any range comparison.

Most comments add something the code can't show, such as why GROUND_Y is a constant instead of being read from the part and why the overlap box is shrunk, but 'Max distance from the player's HumanoidRootPart...' is close to restating the name, and the claim that snap can produce inf/NaN near the float limit is doubtful.
The file opens with a nine-line header block that mostly repeats the task, and several multi-line comments (the GROUND_Y note, the `check` doc) could be shorter.
The docs for `snap`, `snapFromHit` and `check` say what the returns mean and what input each expects without listing parameters, though `check`'s doc runs long.

criteria.criterion: No change history or external references
criteria.note: There is no change history; the pointer to default.project.json names a file in the repo the reader can open, so it is acceptable.
It is a single frozen shared module with no remote or UI and it passes all checks; the bare tuple return `(boolean, string?, Vector3?)` is typed less tightly than a tagged union would be.

`validatePlacement` covers every rule: it checks the five types, computes ground height from the Baseplate top, uses MAX_LAYER = 200//4 - 1 for the height cap, enforces 24-stud reach on the snapped center, and runs an AABB overlap test with OVERLAP_TOLERANCE so neighbours pass; `snapToGrid` and `getCellFromHit` are exposed.
It checks `typeof(position) ~= "Vector3" or not isFiniteVector3(position)` before computing the layer, and the comparison-based `isFinite` rejects NaN and both infinities.
Each comment carries a real reason: the overlap-tolerance float note, the NaN-comparison gotcha, the unrotated-Baseplate assumption, and why re-snapping a cell center is safe on the server.
There is no file header or banner, the comments are short and sit next to the code they govern, and the doc blocks are only a few lines each.
The docs for `validatePlacement`, `snapToGrid`, `getCellFromHit` and `getGroundHeight` state behavior and assumptions; `isBlockType` has no doc, which is acceptable because it is self-explanatory.

criteria.criterion: No change history or external references
criteria.note: The comments describe only the current code and contain no history or outside references.

It is a strictly typed shared module with a tagged-union `PlacementResult` and it passes the checks, but the manual overlap loop only looks at direct BasePart children and assumes the parts are axis-aligned.

strengths: Uses the engine's spatial query, so blocks nested anywhere inside the folder are caught
Finiteness checks are thorough and run before any range check
Doc comment warns not to parent the ghost preview to the blocks folder
weaknesses: The file-header block is boilerplate and long
Several comments are wordier than they need to be
The tuple return type is looser than a result type

strengths: The tagged-union result type is clean and easy for callers to use
Comments are tight and every one explains a reason
Ground height comes from the actual Baseplate, and RootPart is passed in through the context so callers can supply it
weaknesses: The overlap check skips blocks that are nested in Models or rotated
Block-type casing is capitalized, which the task did not specify
Callers have to supply a Baseplate reference on every call
